mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the federal funds rate over the past three months compresses discount rates for equity valuation, producing positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days as monetary policy eases.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of periods when FEDFUNDS declines for 3 months, or Rank IC falls below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate exceeds 4.5% for two consecutive months, it signals aggressive monetary tightening that increases equity discount rates and reduces valuations, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of periods when FEDFUNDS > 4.5% for 2 consecutive months, or Rank IC remains below 0.03 over 3 years.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous decline in unemployment rate and increase in payroll employment signals robust labor market conditions that boost corporate earnings and consumer spending, driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: The interaction between UNRATE decline and PAYEMS increase fails to predict positive 5-day returns in more than 60% of instances, or interaction term Rank IC < 0.03 over 3 years.

mechanism_narrative: In a late-cycle expansion regime, housing starts below 1000 thousand units signal weakening consumer demand and rising recession risks, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are positive in more than 60% of periods when HOUST < 1000 during late-cycle expansion, or Rank IC < 0.03 over 3 years.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in industrial production above 102.0 for three consecutive months indicates robust supply chain conditions and rising corporate output, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of periods when INDPRO > 102.0 for 3 months, or Rank IC < 0.03 over 3 years.

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate rises above 6.5% for two consecutive months, it signals labor market deterioration that reduces consumer spending and corporate profits, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of periods when UNRATE > 6.5% for 2 consecutive months, or Rank IC < 0.03 over 3 years.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous decline in CPI inflation and increase in retail sales (RSAFS) signals stable demand conditions that support corporate pricing power and earnings growth, driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: The interaction between CPIAUCSL decline and RSAFS increase fails to predict positive 5-day returns in more than 60% of instances, or interaction term Rank IC < 0.03 over 3 years.

mechanism_narrative: During a monetary tightening cycle, a decline in the federal funds rate relative to its 10-year moving average signals policy reversal, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 days as market expectations shift.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are negative in more than 60% of periods when FEDFUNDS declines relative to 10-year MA during tightening cycle, or Rank IC < 0.03 over 3 years.
